correctness.rationale: The necessary-and-sufficient gap condition is proved by considering both routes between consecutive terminals and observing that all terminal-terminal paths are unions of full gaps. A positive-weight cycle has at most one gap heavier than half the circumference, and a shortest route cannot consist of that gap alone. Factorization, extremizer count, cyclotomic zero set and Toeplitz-convolution log-concavity follow rigorously. The independent finite distance verifier passed 340304 unweighted and 333120 weighted terminal/deletion comparisons (not used as infinite proof). All quantifiers n>=3, 2<=|T|<=n, and arbitrary finite positive real lengths are justified.

value.rationale: The new semi-cutting parameter raises an explicit equality-case and minimum-edge-transversal question. For every position of two or more terminals on a natural positively weighted cycle, the result answers exact minimum, counts each feasible deletion cardinality, identifies nonseparating optima, and determines the full root locus and coefficient log-concavity. The half-circumference transition survives all positive real weights and is a structural boundary, not a one-off small graph or arbitrary slice.
